scripts.//secrets:check: Layer 3 of the credential gate, and the only layer that cannot be skipped: every credential-shaped key in every tracked config file must be BLANK at HEAD. The key set is derived from Diag.SECRET_PATTERNS in tLib (one list, parsed out of the Lua that the runtime redactor uses) rather than hand-listed -- a four-name array is exactly how Advanced.S3.AccessKey went uncovered. Layer 1 is .githooks/pre-commit, which refuses the commit; layer 2 blanks the staged copy of a release. The real value lives in the gitignored config.local.lua sidecar, so there is nothing to strip and nothing a `git pull` can overwrite. Exit 1 = a credential has a value; exit 2 = the gate could not run, which is NOT a pass.
scripts.//prod: Cuts .build/tChirp.zip from an explicit include ALLOWLIST. Both directions are checked: stageFiles throws on a listed path that has stopped existing, assertManifestStaged throws on a path fxmanifest.lua declares that nobody added to the list -- a release that builds clean and then fails at load on a customer's server, reported to the player rather than to whoever cut it. Then checkStagedTree asserts no runtime state reached the archive. tChirp has none today, which is exactly why the gate runs: the allowlist is what keeps that true and an allowlist is edited by hand.
scripts.//test:lua:control: Negative control for the Lua gate. Three cases: a suite whose assertion is FALSE and a suite that raises on its first statement (both must exit non-zero), plus discovery over a directory that exists and holds no .lua (must find nothing). Case 2 is the hazard run-lua-suite.lua exists for -- MEASURED: `fengari scripts/controls/lua/lua-throws.lua` prints the error and exits 0, while the same file through the shim exits 1. Scoped to the harness deliberately: all three suites under scripts/tests already assert both directions of every rule, so a dead validator trips one half of a pair, whereas nothing else measures whether a failing suite goes red at all.
scripts.//check:syntax: Parses EVERY Lua file in the resource with `loadfile`, which compiles and never runs. `bun test` loads no Lua at all and the fengari suites only load the four files they are oracles for, so a missing `end` anywhere else first surfaced as a resource that REFUSES TO START on a live server. Exit 2 = found no files, which is NOT a pass.
scripts.//check:syntax:control: Negative control for check:syntax. Three cases: a fixture with a missing `end` (must exit 1), a directory with no Lua in it (must exit 2 -- a gate that cannot measure must not report a pass), and tChirp's real source tree, which must stay GREEN. The decoy is not optional: a harness that has stopped reading exit codes reports every case as failing, which is what a correct run of the two red cases looks like.
scripts.//docs:check: Validates docs/ before .gitea/workflows/docs.yml publishes it. That workflow is a PUSH -- it replaces src/content/docs/tChirp/ in tWeb wholesale and pushes -- and the site's own CI runs only AFTER that has landed, so a broken page is already live by the time anything notices. tChirp's pages carry five cross-page anchor links, which is exactly what a renamed heading silently breaks. Exit 1 on an empty docs/content: every check in it is green on zero pages.
scripts.//docs:check:control: Negative control for docs:check. Every check in it is a regex over MDX, and a regex that stops matching reports nothing rather than reporting a problem -- so this kills one named scanner at a time and requires the report to change. It carries its own floor: with zero cross-page links in the docs the `page` case is satisfied by a gate that does nothing, so a clean run finding none exits 1 rather than passing.
scripts.//verify: The controls run FIRST, and that order is the point: a gate nobody has watched fail is an assertion, not a gate, and this codebase has repeatedly shipped gates that passed while measuring nothing. Proving the gates can go red before trusting them green costs about four seconds. Then: credentials blank at HEAD, biome, every Lua file parses, the suites pass, the docs are publishable, and the release actually packs. `prod` is last because it is the only link that writes anything.
scripts.verify: bun run secrets:check && bun run test:lua:control && bun run check:syntax:control && bun run docs:check:control && bun run lint && bun run check:syntax && bun run test && bun run docs:check && bun run prod
